q: A hospitalized adult presents with crushing substernal chest pain radiating to left arm/jaw unrelieved by nitroglycerin. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Status Epilepticus
Hypertensive Emergency
Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
COPD Exacerbation
e: Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) (Cardiology) classically presents with crushing substernal chest pain radiating to left arm/jaw unrelieved by nitroglycerin. Confirmation is obtained via 12-lead ecg showing st-segment elevation and elevated cardiac troponin i.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and bilateral pulmonary crackles. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Pancreatitis
Left-Sided Heart Failure
Retinal Detachment
Hypercalcemia (Serum Ca2+ >10.5 mg/dL)
e: Left-Sided Heart Failure (Cardiology) classically presents with dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and bilateral pulmonary crackles. Confirmation is obtained via transthoracic echocardiogram showing reduced lvef and elevated bnp (>100 pg/ml).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with jugular venous distension, dependent pitting edema, hepatomegaly, and ascites. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Tetanus (Clostridium tetani)
Right-Sided Heart Failure (Cor Pulmonale)
Acute Pericarditis
Cardiac Tamponade
e: Right-Sided Heart Failure (Cor Pulmonale) (Cardiology) classically presents with jugular venous distension, dependent pitting edema, hepatomegaly, and ascites. Confirmation is obtained via echocardiography showing right ventricular dilation and elevated pulmonary artery pressure.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with persistent fever, new regurgitant heart murmur, osler nodes, janeway lesions, and roth spots. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Osteomyelitis
Acute Ischemic Stroke
Psoriasis Vulgaris
Infective Endocarditis
e: Infective Endocarditis (Cardiology) classically presents with persistent fever, new regurgitant heart murmur, osler nodes, janeway lesions, and roth spots. Confirmation is obtained via three sets of blood cultures from separate sites plus transesophageal echocardiography (tee).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with beck's triad: hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and distended neck veins with pulsus paradoxus. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Pleural Effusion
Crohn Disease
Hyperkalemia (Serum K+ >5.5 mEq/L)
Cardiac Tamponade
e: Cardiac Tamponade (Cardiology) classically presents with beck's triad: hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and distended neck veins with pulsus paradoxus. Confirmation is obtained via bedside transthoracic echocardiogram showing pericardial effusion with right ventricular diastolic collapse.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with unilateral calf swelling, warmth, erythema, and tenderness along the deep venous system. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans)
HIV / AIDS & Opportunistic Infections
Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
Septic Shock
e: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) (Cardiology) classically presents with unilateral calf swelling, warmth, erythema, and tenderness along the deep venous system. Confirmation is obtained via venous duplex compression ultrasonography and d-dimer assay.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with sudden-onset pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea, tachycardia, hemoptysis, and unexplained hypoxemia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) & TURP
Bacterial Meningitis
Ulcerative Colitis
Acute Pulmonary Embolism
e: Acute Pulmonary Embolism (Pulmonology) classically presents with sudden-onset pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea, tachycardia, hemoptysis, and unexplained hypoxemia. Confirmation is obtained via ct pulmonary angiography (ctpa).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with sharp pleuritic substernal chest pain relieved by leaning forward and pericardial friction rub. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Pericarditis
Tetanus (Clostridium tetani)
Trigeminal Neuralgia (Tic Douloureux)
Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
e: Acute Pericarditis (Cardiology) classically presents with sharp pleuritic substernal chest pain relieved by leaning forward and pericardial friction rub. Confirmation is obtained via 12-lead ecg showing diffuse concave st-segment elevation and pr-segment depression.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with severely elevated bp (>180/120 mmhg) accompanied by acute target-organ damage (encephalopathy, papilledema, aki). Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Status Epilepticus
Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Active)
Hypertensive Emergency
Anaphylactic Shock
e: Hypertensive Emergency (Cardiology) classically presents with severely elevated bp (>180/120 mmhg) accompanied by acute target-organ damage (encephalopathy, papilledema, aki). Confirmation is obtained via fundoscopy, 12-lead ecg, serum creatinine, troponin, and head ct if neurological signs present.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with sudden severe 'tearing' chest pain radiating to the interscapular back with asymmetric arm blood pressures. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Pancreatitis
Sickle Cell Crisis (Vaso-Occlusive)
Acute Aortic Dissection
Acute Pericarditis
e: Acute Aortic Dissection (Cardiology) classically presents with sudden severe 'tearing' chest pain radiating to the interscapular back with asymmetric arm blood pressures. Confirmation is obtained via ct angiography of the chest and abdomen (or tee if unstable).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with intermittent claudication of feet/hands, rest pain, and digital ulcers in young heavy male smokers. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Trigeminal Neuralgia (Tic Douloureux)
Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)
Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans)
e: Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans) (Cardiology) classically presents with intermittent claudication of feet/hands, rest pain, and digital ulcers in young heavy male smokers. Confirmation is obtained via segmental arterial doppler and angiography showing corkscrew collaterals.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with tortuous dilated superficial leg veins, evening ankle edema, and brownish hemosiderin stasis dermatitis. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA)
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
Right-Sided Heart Failure (Cor Pulmonale)
Varicose Veins & Chronic Venous Insufficiency
e: Varicose Veins & Chronic Venous Insufficiency (Cardiology) classically presents with tortuous dilated superficial leg veins, evening ankle edema, and brownish hemosiderin stasis dermatitis. Confirmation is obtained via venous duplex ultrasound and trendelenburg retrograde filling test.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with worsening dyspnea, barrel chest, pursed-lip breathing, prolonged expiration, and hypercapnia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA)
COPD Exacerbation
Bronchiectasis
Community-Acquired Pneumonia
e: COPD Exacerbation (Pulmonology) classically presents with worsening dyspnea, barrel chest, pursed-lip breathing, prolonged expiration, and hypercapnia. Confirmation is obtained via spirometry showing post-bronchodilator fev1/fvc <0.70 and abg showing respiratory acidosis.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with severe refractory wheezing progressing to a 'silent chest', accessory muscle use, and pulsus paradoxus. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Bell's Palsy (CN VII Paralysis)
Infective Endocarditis
Status Asthmaticus
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
e: Status Asthmaticus (Pulmonology) classically presents with severe refractory wheezing progressing to a 'silent chest', accessory muscle use, and pulsus paradoxus. Confirmation is obtained via peak expiratory flow rate (pefr <40% predicted) and abg showing rising paco2 (impending fatigue).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with absent unilateral breath sounds, hyperresonance to percussion, tracheal deviation to opposite side, and hypotension. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Tension Pneumothorax
Status Asthmaticus
Psoriasis Vulgaris
Hypertensive Emergency
e: Tension Pneumothorax (Pulmonology) classically presents with absent unilateral breath sounds, hyperresonance to percussion, tracheal deviation to opposite side, and hypotension. Confirmation is obtained via clinical diagnosis (do not delay treatment for chest x-ray).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with refractory hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen, bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates ('white-out' lungs). Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Febrile Neutropenia
Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA)
Infective Endocarditis
e: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) (Pulmonology) classically presents with refractory hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen, bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates ('white-out' lungs). Confirmation is obtained via berlin criteria: pao2/fio2 ratio <=300 mmhg with peep >=5 cmh2o and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with productive cough with rusty/purulent sputum, pleuritic pain, fever with chills, and bronchial breath sounds. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Intestinal Obstruction
Community-Acquired Pneumonia
Osteomyelitis
Hypoparathyroidism (Post-Thyroidectomy)
e: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (Pulmonology) classically presents with productive cough with rusty/purulent sputum, pleuritic pain, fever with chills, and bronchial breath sounds. Confirmation is obtained via chest radiograph showing lobar consolidation and sputum gram stain/culture.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with stony dullness to percussion, decreased tactile fremitus, and diminished breath sounds over affected base. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
Acute Kidney Injury (Prerenal/ATN)
Pleural Effusion
COPD Exacerbation
e: Pleural Effusion (Pulmonology) classically presents with stony dullness to percussion, decreased tactile fremitus, and diminished breath sounds over affected base. Confirmation is obtained via chest x-ray showing blunting of costophrenic angle and diagnostic thoracentesis (light's criteria).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with chronic cough >2 weeks, evening rise of fever, drenching night sweats, hemoptysis, and weight loss. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Myxedema Coma
Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
Hypoparathyroidism (Post-Thyroidectomy)
Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Active)
e: Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Active) (Pulmonology) classically presents with chronic cough >2 weeks, evening rise of fever, drenching night sweats, hemoptysis, and weight loss. Confirmation is obtained via sputum afb smear microscopy and cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification test (cbnaat/genexpert).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with chronic cough producing copious foul-smelling three-layered sputum and digital clubbing. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans)
COPD Exacerbation
Thyroid Storm (Thyrotoxic Crisis)
Bronchiectasis
e: Bronchiectasis (Pulmonology) classically presents with chronic cough producing copious foul-smelling three-layered sputum and digital clubbing. Confirmation is obtained via high-resolution ct (hrct) chest showing 'signet-ring' dilated airways.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with sudden unilateral hemiparesis, facial droop, aphasia/dysarthria, and homonymous hemianopia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)
Meniere Disease
Ulcerative Colitis
Acute Ischemic Stroke
e: Acute Ischemic Stroke (Neurology) classically presents with sudden unilateral hemiparesis, facial droop, aphasia/dysarthria, and homonymous hemianopia. Confirmation is obtained via immediate non-contrast head ct to rule out intracranial hemorrhage before thrombolysis.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with cushing's triad (widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, irregular respirations), papilledema, and declining gcs. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Autonomic Dysreflexia (SCI above T6)
Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)
Acute Glomerulonephritis (Post-Streptococcal)
Increased Intracranial Pressure (ICP)
e: Increased Intracranial Pressure (ICP) (Neurology) classically presents with cushing's triad (widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, irregular respirations), papilledema, and declining gcs. Confirmation is obtained via intraventricular catheter (evd) icp monitoring (>20 mmhg sustained) and head ct.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with high fever, severe headache, nuchal rigidity, photophobia, positive kernig's and brudzinski's signs. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Bacterial Meningitis
Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS)
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
Hypertensive Emergency
e: Bacterial Meningitis (Neurology) classically presents with high fever, severe headache, nuchal rigidity, photophobia, positive kernig's and brudzinski's signs. Confirmation is obtained via lumbar puncture csf analysis showing high neutrophils, high protein, and low glucose (<40 mg/dl).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness worsening with exertion, ptosis, diplopia, and dysphagia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever
Pleural Effusion
Bronchiectasis
Myasthenia Gravis
e: Myasthenia Gravis (Neurology) classically presents with fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness worsening with exertion, ptosis, diplopia, and dysphagia. Confirmation is obtained via anti-acetylcholine receptor (achr) antibody assay and tensilon (edrophonium)/ice-pack test.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with rapidly progressive symmetric ascending flaccid paralysis with areflexia following respiratory/gi infection. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Hypoparathyroidism (Post-Thyroidectomy)
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
Psoriasis Vulgaris
Guillain-Barre Syndrome (GBS)
e: Guillain-Barre Syndrome (GBS) (Neurology) classically presents with rapidly progressive symmetric ascending flaccid paralysis with areflexia following respiratory/gi infection. Confirmation is obtained via csf showing albuminocytologic dissociation (elevated protein with normal wbc count) and nerve conduction study.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with trap tetrad: pill-rolling resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, and postural instability with shuffling gait. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Myxedema Coma
SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
Parkinson Disease
Crohn Disease
e: Parkinson Disease (Neurology) classically presents with trap tetrad: pill-rolling resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, and postural instability with shuffling gait. Confirmation is obtained via clinical diagnosis confirmed by robust motor response to levodopa.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with continuous seizure activity lasting >5 minutes or recurrent seizures without recovery of consciousness. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Sickle Cell Crisis (Vaso-Occlusive)
Status Epilepticus
Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA)
Community-Acquired Pneumonia
e: Status Epilepticus (Neurology) classically presents with continuous seizure activity lasting >5 minutes or recurrent seizures without recovery of consciousness. Confirmation is obtained via bedside capillary glucose, serum electrolytes, anticonvulsant levels, and continuous eeg.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with sudden severe paroxysmal hypertension, pounding headache, flushed skin above injury, and bradycardia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Autonomic Dysreflexia (SCI above T6)
COPD Exacerbation
Rheumatoid Arthritis
Hyponatremia (Serum Na+ <135 mEq/L)
e: Autonomic Dysreflexia (SCI above T6) (Neurology) classically presents with sudden severe paroxysmal hypertension, pounding headache, flushed skin above injury, and bradycardia. Confirmation is obtained via immediate blood pressure measurement and assessment for noxious stimulus below t6 (distended bladder/bowel).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with brief electric-shock-like unilateral facial pain along cn v maxillary/mandibular branches triggered by light touch. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Rheumatoid Arthritis
Increased Intracranial Pressure (ICP)
Trigeminal Neuralgia (Tic Douloureux)
Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA)
e: Trigeminal Neuralgia (Tic Douloureux) (Neurology) classically presents with brief electric-shock-like unilateral facial pain along cn v maxillary/mandibular branches triggered by light touch. Confirmation is obtained via clinical history plus brain mri to rule out vascular compression or demyelination.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with acute unilateral upper and lower facial weakness with inability to close the ipsilateral eye and loss of nasolabial fold. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Pheochromocytoma
Bell's Palsy (CN VII Paralysis)
Right-Sided Heart Failure (Cor Pulmonale)
Addisonian Crisis (Acute Adrenal Insufficiency)
e: Bell's Palsy (CN VII Paralysis) (Neurology) classically presents with acute unilateral upper and lower facial weakness with inability to close the ipsilateral eye and loss of nasolabial fold. Confirmation is obtained via clinical exclusion of central stroke (forehead is spared in stroke but paralyzed in bell's palsy).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with polyuria, polydipsia, kussmaul deep rapid respirations, fruity acetone breath, and abdominal pain. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
Psoriasis Vulgaris
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Septic Shock
e: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) (Endocrinology) classically presents with polyuria, polydipsia, kussmaul deep rapid respirations, fruity acetone breath, and abdominal pain. Confirmation is obtained via blood glucose >250 mg/dl, arterial ph <7.30, hco3 <18 meq/l, and positive serum/urine ketones.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with profound dehydration, altered sensorium/coma, and extreme hyperglycemia without significant ketoacidosis in type 2 dm. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans)
Acute Pancreatitis
Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS)
e: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS) (Endocrinology) classically presents with profound dehydration, altered sensorium/coma, and extreme hyperglycemia without significant ketoacidosis in type 2 dm. Confirmation is obtained via blood glucose >600 mg/dl, serum osmolality >320 mosm/kg, arterial ph >7.30, and minimal ketones.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with extreme hyperpyrexia (>40 c), severe tachycardia (>140 bpm), agitation/delirium, and high-output heart failure. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
Ulcerative Colitis
Thyroid Storm (Thyrotoxic Crisis)
Myasthenia Gravis
e: Thyroid Storm (Thyrotoxic Crisis) (Endocrinology) classically presents with extreme hyperpyrexia (>40 c), severe tachycardia (>140 bpm), agitation/delirium, and high-output heart failure. Confirmation is obtained via markedly suppressed tsh with elevated free t3/t4 and burch-wartofsky clinical score.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with profound hypothermia, bradycardia, hypoventilation, hyponatremia, and obtundation in untreated hypothyroidism. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Intestinal Obstruction
Myxedema Coma
Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)
Cushing Syndrome
e: Myxedema Coma (Endocrinology) classically presents with profound hypothermia, bradycardia, hypoventilation, hyponatremia, and obtundation in untreated hypothyroidism. Confirmation is obtained via markedly elevated tsh with severely low free t4 and hyponatremia.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with refractory hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia, and bronze hyperpigmentation. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Pulmonary Embolism
Addisonian Crisis (Acute Adrenal Insufficiency)
Iron Deficiency Anemia
Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / TEN
e: Addisonian Crisis (Acute Adrenal Insufficiency) (Endocrinology) classically presents with refractory hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia, and bronze hyperpigmentation. Confirmation is obtained via low morning serum cortisol, elevated acth, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with moon face, buffalo hump, central truncal obesity, purple abdominal striae, hypertension, and hyperglycemia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Cushing Syndrome
Tumor Lysis Syndrome (Oncology Emergency)
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Peptic Ulcer Disease (Duodenal vs Gastric)
e: Cushing Syndrome (Endocrinology) classically presents with moon face, buffalo hump, central truncal obesity, purple abdominal striae, hypertension, and hyperglycemia. Confirmation is obtained via 24-hour urinary free cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol, and low-dose dexamethasone suppression test.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with paroxysmal triad of pounding headache, profuse diaphoresis, and palpitations with severe episodic hypertension. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
Hypertensive Emergency
Pheochromocytoma
e: Pheochromocytoma (Endocrinology) classically presents with paroxysmal triad of pounding headache, profuse diaphoresis, and palpitations with severe episodic hypertension. Confirmation is obtained via 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines and plasma free metanephrines plus adrenal ct/mri.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with euvolemic hyponatremia, concentrated dark urine, weight gain without edema, and confusion/seizures. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Bacterial Meningitis
Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
Psoriasis Vulgaris
SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
e: SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH) (Endocrinology) classically presents with euvolemic hyponatremia, concentrated dark urine, weight gain without edema, and confusion/seizures. Confirmation is obtained via serum sodium <135 meq/l, low serum osmolality (<275), and inappropriately high urine osmolality (>100).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with massive polyuria (>4–10 l/day of pale dilute urine), intense polydipsia, and hypernatremia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) & TURP
Diabetes Insipidus (Central)
Myasthenia Gravis
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
e: Diabetes Insipidus (Central) (Endocrinology) classically presents with massive polyuria (>4–10 l/day of pale dilute urine), intense polydipsia, and hypernatremia. Confirmation is obtained via water deprivation test showing failure to concentrate urine (specific gravity <1.005) responding to desmopressin.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with perioral numbness, carpopedal spasm, positive chvostek's and trousseau's signs, and laryngeal stridor. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
Diabetes Insipidus (Central)
HIV / AIDS & Opportunistic Infections
Hypoparathyroidism (Post-Thyroidectomy)
e: Hypoparathyroidism (Post-Thyroidectomy) (Endocrinology) classically presents with perioral numbness, carpopedal spasm, positive chvostek's and trousseau's signs, and laryngeal stridor. Confirmation is obtained via low serum calcium (<8.5 mg/dl), high serum phosphorus, low pth, and prolonged qt interval on ecg.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with oliguria (<400 ml/day), rising bun/creatinine, fluid overload, metabolic acidosis, and hyperkalemia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Fat Embolism Syndrome (Long-Bone Fracture)
Myasthenia Gravis
Acute Kidney Injury (Prerenal/ATN)
Varicose Veins & Chronic Venous Insufficiency
e: Acute Kidney Injury (Prerenal/ATN) (Nephrology) classically presents with oliguria (<400 ml/day), rising bun/creatinine, fluid overload, metabolic acidosis, and hyperkalemia. Confirmation is obtained via kdigo criteria (creatinine rise >=0.3 mg/dl in 48h), urine microscopy showing muddy brown granular casts in atn.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with uremic frost, pruritus, anemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, metabolic acidosis, and hypertension. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 5 / ESRD)
SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
Tetanus (Clostridium tetani)
Status Asthmaticus
e: Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 5 / ESRD) (Nephrology) classically presents with uremic frost, pruritus, anemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, metabolic acidosis, and hypertension. Confirmation is obtained via egfr <15 ml/min/1.73m2 for >3 months and small echogenic kidneys on ultrasound.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with massive proteinuria (>3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminemia, severe periorbital/generalized anasarca, and hyperlipidemia. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Retinal Detachment
Nephrotic Syndrome
Acute Appendicitis
Ulcerative Colitis
e: Nephrotic Syndrome (Nephrology) classically presents with massive proteinuria (>3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminemia, severe periorbital/generalized anasarca, and hyperlipidemia. Confirmation is obtained via 24-hour urine protein >3.5 g, urine oval fat bodies, and renal biopsy for histology.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with cola/tea-colored gross hematuria, periorbital edema, hypertension, and oliguria 1–3 weeks after strep throat. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Hypokalemia (Serum K+ <3.5 mEq/L)
Infective Endocarditis
Acute Glomerulonephritis (Post-Streptococcal)
Myasthenia Gravis
e: Acute Glomerulonephritis (Post-Streptococcal) (Nephrology) classically presents with cola/tea-colored gross hematuria, periorbital edema, hypertension, and oliguria 1–3 weeks after strep throat. Confirmation is obtained via urinalysis showing rbc casts and dysmorphic rbcs, elevated aso titer, and low c3 complement.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with excruciating colicky flank pain radiating to the groin/labia/testis with microscopic or gross hematuria. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Status Asthmaticus
Urolithiasis (Renal Calculi)
Acute Kidney Injury (Prerenal/ATN)
Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
e: Urolithiasis (Renal Calculi) (Nephrology) classically presents with excruciating colicky flank pain radiating to the groin/labia/testis with microscopic or gross hematuria. Confirmation is obtained via non-contrast helical ct of abdomen and pelvis (kub).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with urinary hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia, incomplete emptying, and dribbling in older men. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Aortic Dissection
Hypercalcemia (Serum Ca2+ >10.5 mg/dL)
Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS)
Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) & TURP
e: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) & TURP (Nephrology) classically presents with urinary hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia, incomplete emptying, and dribbling in older men. Confirmation is obtained via digital rectal exam showing smooth symmetrical enlargement, psa to exclude cancer, and post-void residual volume.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with epigastric burning pain relieved by food (duodenal) or worsened shortly after meals (gastric). Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency)
Cataract & Post-Cataract Surgery
Status Epilepticus
Peptic Ulcer Disease (Duodenal vs Gastric)
e: Peptic Ulcer Disease (Duodenal vs Gastric) (Gastroenterology) classically presents with epigastric burning pain relieved by food (duodenal) or worsened shortly after meals (gastric). Confirmation is obtained via upper gi endoscopy (egd) with biopsy and h. pylori urea breath or stool antigen test.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with jaundice, ascites, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, caput medusae, and asterixis (flapping tremor). Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Left-Sided Heart Failure
Hepatic Cirrhosis & Portal Hypertension
Crohn Disease
Hyperkalemia (Serum K+ >5.5 mEq/L)
e: Hepatic Cirrhosis & Portal Hypertension (Gastroenterology) classically presents with jaundice, ascites, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, caput medusae, and asterixis (flapping tremor). Confirmation is obtained via elevated bilirubin/inr, low albumin, abdominal ultrasound, and fibroscan/liver biopsy.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with severe boring epigastric pain radiating straight to the back, cullen's sign (periumbilical) and grey turner's sign (flank). Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency)
Parkinson Disease
Meniere Disease
Acute Pancreatitis
e: Acute Pancreatitis (Gastroenterology) classically presents with severe boring epigastric pain radiating straight to the back, cullen's sign (periumbilical) and grey turner's sign (flank). Confirmation is obtained via serum lipase (>3x upper limit of normal — most specific) and contrast-enhanced abdominal ct.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with right upper quadrant pain radiating to right scapula after fatty meals with positive murphy's sign. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA)
Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)
Acute Cholecystitis
Acute Ischemic Stroke
e: Acute Cholecystitis (Gastroenterology) classically presents with right upper quadrant pain radiating to right scapula after fatty meals with positive murphy's sign. Confirmation is obtained via right upper quadrant abdominal ultrasound showing gallstones, thickened wall (>3 mm), and pericholecystic fluid.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with periumbilical pain migrating to mcburney's point in rlq with rebound tenderness, rovsing's and psoas signs. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Intestinal Obstruction
Acute Appendicitis
HIV / AIDS & Opportunistic Infections
Anaphylactic Shock
e: Acute Appendicitis (Gastroenterology) classically presents with periumbilical pain migrating to mcburney's point in rlq with rebound tenderness, rovsing's and psoas signs. Confirmation is obtained via abdominal ct (adults) or graded-compression ultrasound (children/pregnancy) with leukocytosis.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with colicky abdominal pain, bilious/feculent vomiting, obstipation (no flatus/stool), and high-pitched tinkling bowel sounds. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate ADH)
Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) & TURP
Pheochromocytoma
Intestinal Obstruction
e: Intestinal Obstruction (Gastroenterology) classically presents with colicky abdominal pain, bilious/feculent vomiting, obstipation (no flatus/stool), and high-pitched tinkling bowel sounds. Confirmation is obtained via upright abdominal x-ray showing multiple air-fluid levels and dilated bowel loops.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with frequent bloody mucoid diarrhea (10–20 stools/day), tenesmus, and llq cramping limited to colonic mucosa. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
Anaphylactic Shock
Ulcerative Colitis
e: Ulcerative Colitis (Gastroenterology) classically presents with frequent bloody mucoid diarrhea (10–20 stools/day), tenesmus, and llq cramping limited to colonic mucosa. Confirmation is obtained via colonoscopy showing continuous mucosal ulceration/pseudopolyps from rectum proximally and lead-pipe barium enema.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with rlq pain, chronic non-bloody diarrhea, weight loss, perianal fistulas, and transmural 'skip lesions'. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Crohn Disease
Acute Aortic Dissection
Autonomic Dysreflexia (SCI above T6)
Meniere Disease
e: Crohn Disease (Gastroenterology) classically presents with rlq pain, chronic non-bloody diarrhea, weight loss, perianal fistulas, and transmural 'skip lesions'. Confirmation is obtained via ileocolonoscopy showing cobblestone mucosa, skip lesions, and non-caseating granulomas on biopsy.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with fatigue, pallor, koilonychia (spoon-shaped nails), glossitis, angular cheilitis, and pica. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Pleural Effusion
Status Asthmaticus
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Iron Deficiency Anemia
e: Iron Deficiency Anemia (Hematology) classically presents with fatigue, pallor, koilonychia (spoon-shaped nails), glossitis, angular cheilitis, and pica. Confirmation is obtained via microcytic hypochromic rbcs on smear, low serum ferritin (most sensitive), and high tibc.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with beefy red smooth tongue, fatigue, and symmetrical paresthesias with loss of vibration/proprioception. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Megaloblastic Anemia (Vitamin B12 Deficiency)
Septic Shock
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
Intestinal Obstruction
e: Megaloblastic Anemia (Vitamin B12 Deficiency) (Hematology) classically presents with beefy red smooth tongue, fatigue, and symmetrical paresthesias with loss of vibration/proprioception. Confirmation is obtained via macrocytic anemia (mcv >100 fl), hypersegmented neutrophils, low serum b12, and elevated methylmalonic acid.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with severe acute bone/joint/chest pain triggered by hypoxia, dehydration, cold, or infection. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Sickle Cell Crisis (Vaso-Occlusive)
Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
Ulcerative Colitis
HIV / AIDS & Opportunistic Infections
e: Sickle Cell Crisis (Vaso-Occlusive) (Hematology) classically presents with severe acute bone/joint/chest pain triggered by hypoxia, dehydration, cold, or infection. Confirmation is obtained via hemoglobin electrophoresis showing hbs and peripheral smear showing sickled erythrocytes.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with spontaneous hemarthrosis (painful swollen knees/elbows) and prolonged bleeding after minor trauma. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Hip Fracture & Total Hip Arthroplasty
Crohn Disease
Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency)
Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
e: Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency) (Hematology) classically presents with spontaneous hemarthrosis (painful swollen knees/elbows) and prolonged bleeding after minor trauma. Confirmation is obtained via prolonged aptt with normal pt, normal platelet count, and low factor viii assay.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with simultaneous widespread microvascular thrombosis and profuse oozing from iv sites, gums, and surgical wounds. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
Septic Shock
Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)
e: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC) (Hematology) classically presents with simultaneous widespread microvascular thrombosis and profuse oozing from iv sites, gums, and surgical wounds. Confirmation is obtained via thrombocytopenia, prolonged pt and aptt, low fibrinogen, and markedly elevated d-dimer/fdps.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hyperuricemia, and secondary hypocalcemia shortly after initiating chemotherapy. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Cardiac Tamponade
Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
Tumor Lysis Syndrome (Oncology Emergency)
Thyroid Storm (Thyrotoxic Crisis)
e: Tumor Lysis Syndrome (Oncology Emergency) (Oncology) classically presents with hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hyperuricemia, and secondary hypocalcemia shortly after initiating chemotherapy. Confirmation is obtained via serial serum uric acid, potassium, phosphate, calcium, and creatinine levels.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with single oral temperature >=38.3 c (or >=38.0 c for 1 hr) with absolute neutrophil count (anc) <500/mm3. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)
Pulmonary Tuberculosis (Active)
Febrile Neutropenia
Trigeminal Neuralgia (Tic Douloureux)
e: Febrile Neutropenia (Oncology) classically presents with single oral temperature >=38.3 c (or >=38.0 c for 1 hr) with absolute neutrophil count (anc) <500/mm3. Confirmation is obtained via cbc with differential (anc <500), two sets of blood cultures, and chest x-ray.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with partial/full-thickness skin destruction, hypovolemic burn shock, and singed nasal hairs/sooty sputum in inhalation injury. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA)
Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
Pulmonary Edema (Acute Cardiogenic)
Bacterial Meningitis
e: Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA) (Trauma) classically presents with partial/full-thickness skin destruction, hypovolemic burn shock, and singed nasal hairs/sooty sputum in inhalation injury. Confirmation is obtained via rule of nines tbsa calculation, carboxyhemoglobin level, and bronchoscopy if inhalation injury suspected.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with severe pain out of proportion to injury unrelieved by opioids and exacerbated by passive stretching of fingers/toes. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: COPD Exacerbation
Compartment Syndrome (Orthopedic Emergency)
Acute Cholecystitis
Myasthenia Gravis
e: Compartment Syndrome (Orthopedic Emergency) (Orthopedics) classically presents with severe pain out of proportion to injury unrelieved by opioids and exacerbated by passive stretching of fingers/toes. Confirmation is obtained via intracompartmental pressure measurement (>30 mmhg) alongside clinical 6 ps assessment.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with classic triad 24–72 hours post-femur fracture: acute hypoxemia/dyspnea, neurological confusion, and petechial rash on chest/axilla. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Aortic Dissection
Status Asthmaticus
Fat Embolism Syndrome (Long-Bone Fracture)
Community-Acquired Pneumonia
e: Fat Embolism Syndrome (Long-Bone Fracture) (Orthopedics) classically presents with classic triad 24–72 hours post-femur fracture: acute hypoxemia/dyspnea, neurological confusion, and petechial rash on chest/axilla. Confirmation is obtained via clinical gurd's criteria, abg showing severe hypoxemia (pao2 <60 mmhg), and chest x-ray 'snowstorm' infiltrate.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with shortened, adducted, and externally rotated affected leg after a fall in an older adult. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Retinal Detachment
Hip Fracture & Total Hip Arthroplasty
Infective Endocarditis
Acute Kidney Injury (Prerenal/ATN)
e: Hip Fracture & Total Hip Arthroplasty (Orthopedics) classically presents with shortened, adducted, and externally rotated affected leg after a fall in an older adult. Confirmation is obtained via ap and lateral pelvic/hip radiographs.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with deep throbbing localized bone pain, fever, erythema, and draining sinus tract. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Urolithiasis (Renal Calculi)
Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans)
Myxedema Coma
Osteomyelitis
e: Osteomyelitis (Orthopedics) classically presents with deep throbbing localized bone pain, fever, erythema, and draining sinus tract. Confirmation is obtained via mri of affected bone (most sensitive early imaging) and bone biopsy with culture.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with symmetric morning joint stiffness >1 hour affecting mcp/pip joints, ulnar deviation, and swan-neck/boutonniere deformities. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Rheumatoid Arthritis
Acute Pulmonary Embolism
Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / TEN
Bacterial Meningitis
e: Rheumatoid Arthritis (Immunology) classically presents with symmetric morning joint stiffness >1 hour affecting mcp/pip joints, ulnar deviation, and swan-neck/boutonniere deformities. Confirmation is obtained via anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-ccp — most specific) and rheumatoid factor (rf) with elevated esr/crp.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with malar butterfly rash across cheeks sparing nasolabial folds, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and polyarthritis. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Bronchiectasis
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
Tumor Lysis Syndrome (Oncology Emergency)
Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC)
e: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) (Immunology) classically presents with malar butterfly rash across cheeks sparing nasolabial folds, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and polyarthritis. Confirmation is obtained via ana (most sensitive screening) and anti-dsdna / anti-smith antibodies (most specific).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with sudden excruciating swollen erythematous first metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra) often waking patient at night. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)
Guillain-Barre Syndrome (GBS)
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
e: Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis) (Immunology) classically presents with sudden excruciating swollen erythematous first metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra) often waking patient at night. Confirmation is obtained via joint fluid aspiration showing needle-shaped negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with rapid onset urticaria, angioedema, stridor/wheezing, and profound distributive hypotension minutes after allergen exposure. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Tension Pneumothorax
COPD Exacerbation
Anaphylactic Shock
Ulcerative Colitis
e: Anaphylactic Shock (Immunology) classically presents with rapid onset urticaria, angioedema, stridor/wheezing, and profound distributive hypotension minutes after allergen exposure. Confirmation is obtained via clinical diagnosis (elevated serum tryptase confirms retrospectively — never delay epinephrine).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with suspected infection with persistent hypotension (map <65 mmhg) despite fluids and serum lactate >2 mmol/l. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Cushing Syndrome
Crohn Disease
Status Epilepticus
Septic Shock
e: Septic Shock (Critical Care) classically presents with suspected infection with persistent hypotension (map <65 mmhg) despite fluids and serum lactate >2 mmol/l. Confirmation is obtained via two sets of blood cultures, serum lactate, procalcitonin, and sofa score >=2.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with painless gradual bilateral loss of peripheral 'tunnel' vision with optic disc cupping. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
Hyperkalemia (Serum K+ >5.5 mEq/L)
Compartment Syndrome (Orthopedic Emergency)
Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
e: Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma (Ophthalmology) classically presents with painless gradual bilateral loss of peripheral 'tunnel' vision with optic disc cupping. Confirmation is obtained via tonometry showing elevated intraocular pressure (>21 mmhg) and automated perimetry visual field testing.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with sudden severe ocular pain, halos around lights, rock-hard globe, mid-dilated fixed pupil, and nausea/vomiting. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 5 / ESRD)
Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma
Rheumatoid Arthritis
Right-Sided Heart Failure (Cor Pulmonale)
e: Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma (Ophthalmology) classically presents with sudden severe ocular pain, halos around lights, rock-hard globe, mid-dilated fixed pupil, and nausea/vomiting. Confirmation is obtained via emergent slit-lamp exam and tonometry showing acutely elevated iop (often >40–60 mmhg).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with sudden shower of floaters, flashes of light (photopsia), and painless 'curtain' descending across visual field. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Retinal Detachment
Hypokalemia (Serum K+ <3.5 mEq/L)
Left-Sided Heart Failure
Cataract & Post-Cataract Surgery
e: Retinal Detachment (Ophthalmology) classically presents with sudden shower of floaters, flashes of light (photopsia), and painless 'curtain' descending across visual field. Confirmation is obtained via dilated indirect ophthalmoscopy.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with episodic triad of severe spinning vertigo, unilateral fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, and roaring tinnitus. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Meniere Disease
Hyponatremia (Serum Na+ <135 mEq/L)
Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency)
Osteomyelitis
e: Meniere Disease (ENT) classically presents with episodic triad of severe spinning vertigo, unilateral fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, and roaring tinnitus. Confirmation is obtained via audiometry showing low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and clinical exclusion of acoustic neuroma.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with painless progressive blurred/cloudy vision, decreased color perception, and glare with night driving. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Right-Sided Heart Failure (Cor Pulmonale)
Cataract & Post-Cataract Surgery
Status Asthmaticus
Increased Intracranial Pressure (ICP)
e: Cataract & Post-Cataract Surgery (Ophthalmology) classically presents with painless progressive blurred/cloudy vision, decreased color perception, and glare with night driving. Confirmation is obtained via slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing lens opacity.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with progressive cd4+ t-cell decline (<200 cells/mm3) predisposing to pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and oral candidiasis. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: HIV / AIDS & Opportunistic Infections
Septic Shock
Myasthenia Gravis
Status Asthmaticus
e: HIV / AIDS & Opportunistic Infections (Infectious Disease) classically presents with progressive cd4+ t-cell decline (<200 cells/mm3) predisposing to pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and oral candidiasis. Confirmation is obtained via 4th-generation hiv ag/ab elisa with confirmatory hiv-1/2 differentiation assay and viral load/cd4 count.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with high 'breakbone' fever, retro-orbital pain, positive tourniquet test, thrombocytopenia, and hemoconcentration. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Thermal Burns (Major >20% TBSA)
Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever
Diabetes Insipidus (Central)
Pulmonary Edema (Acute Cardiogenic)
e: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (Infectious Disease) classically presents with high 'breakbone' fever, retro-orbital pain, positive tourniquet test, thrombocytopenia, and hemoconcentration. Confirmation is obtained via ns1 antigen (days 1–5), igm elisa (after day 5), and serial hematocrit/platelet monitoring.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with trismus (lockjaw), risus sardonicus, painful generalized muscle spasms, and opisthotonus. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Parkinson Disease
Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Tetanus (Clostridium tetani)
Myasthenia Gravis
e: Tetanus (Clostridium tetani) (Infectious Disease) classically presents with trismus (lockjaw), risus sardonicus, painful generalized muscle spasms, and opisthotonus. Confirmation is obtained via clinical diagnosis (wound cultures are frequently negative).

q: A hospitalized adult presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques covered with silvery-white scales on elbows/knees and positive auspitz sign. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Psoriasis Vulgaris
Hemophilia A (Factor VIII Deficiency)
Acute Kidney Injury (Prerenal/ATN)
e: Psoriasis Vulgaris (Dermatology) classically presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques covered with silvery-white scales on elbows/knees and positive auspitz sign. Confirmation is obtained via clinical inspection showing silvery plaques, nail pitting, and koebner phenomenon.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with painful dusky macules progressing to full-thickness epidermal detachment (>30% in ten), mucosal erosions, and positive nikolsky sign. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / TEN
Bronchiectasis
Pleural Effusion
Meniere Disease
e: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / TEN (Dermatology) classically presents with painful dusky macules progressing to full-thickness epidermal detachment (>30% in ten), mucosal erosions, and positive nikolsky sign. Confirmation is obtained via clinical exam plus skin biopsy showing full-thickness epidermal necrosis.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with muscle weakness, paralytic ileus, flattened/inverted t waves, st depression, and prominent u waves on ecg. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Hyperkalemia (Serum K+ >5.5 mEq/L)
Sickle Cell Crisis (Vaso-Occlusive)
Autonomic Dysreflexia (SCI above T6)
Hypokalemia (Serum K+ <3.5 mEq/L)
e: Hypokalemia (Serum K+ <3.5 mEq/L) (Fluid & Electrolytes) classically presents with muscle weakness, paralytic ileus, flattened/inverted t waves, st depression, and prominent u waves on ecg. Confirmation is obtained via serum potassium <3.5 meq/l and 12-lead ecg.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with tall peaked tented t waves, prolonged pr interval, widened qrs complex, and ascending muscle weakness. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Hyperkalemia (Serum K+ >5.5 mEq/L)
Varicose Veins & Chronic Venous Insufficiency
Psoriasis Vulgaris
Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) & TURP
e: Hyperkalemia (Serum K+ >5.5 mEq/L) (Fluid & Electrolytes) classically presents with tall peaked tented t waves, prolonged pr interval, widened qrs complex, and ascending muscle weakness. Confirmation is obtained via serum potassium >5.5 meq/l (confirm non-hemolyzed sample) and immediate 12-lead ecg.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with lethargy, confusion, nausea, headache, and generalized seizures from cerebral cellular swelling. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
Pleural Effusion
Hyponatremia (Serum Na+ <135 mEq/L)
Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / TEN
e: Hyponatremia (Serum Na+ <135 mEq/L) (Fluid & Electrolytes) classically presents with lethargy, confusion, nausea, headache, and generalized seizures from cerebral cellular swelling. Confirmation is obtained via serum sodium <135 meq/l, serum osmolality, urine sodium, and volume status assessment.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with stones (renal calculi), bones (bone pain), abdominal groans (constipation/pancreatitis), and psychiatric overtones with shortened qt. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Myxedema Coma
Acute Appendicitis
Hypercalcemia (Serum Ca2+ >10.5 mg/dL)
Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans)
e: Hypercalcemia (Serum Ca2+ >10.5 mg/dL) (Fluid & Electrolytes) classically presents with stones (renal calculi), bones (bone pain), abdominal groans (constipation/pancreatitis), and psychiatric overtones with shortened qt. Confirmation is obtained via corrected serum calcium >10.5 mg/dl, intact pth, and ecg showing shortened qt interval.

q: A hospitalized adult presents with severe air hunger, sitting bolt upright, tachypnea, cyanosis, and pink frothy sputum. Which Medical-Surgical diagnosis is most strongly indicated?
o: Rheumatoid Arthritis
Pulmonary Edema (Acute Cardiogenic)
Pheochromocytoma
Intestinal Obstruction
e: Pulmonary Edema (Acute Cardiogenic) (Critical Care) classically presents with severe air hunger, sitting bolt upright, tachypnea, cyanosis, and pink frothy sputum. Confirmation is obtained via chest x-ray showing kerley b lines, bat-wing perihilar infiltrates, and cardiomegaly.

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)?
o: Bedside capillary glucose, serum electrolytes, anticonvulsant levels, and continuous EEG
CT angiography of the chest and abdomen (or TEE if unstable)
12-lead ECG showing ST-segment elevation and elevated cardiac Troponin I
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing lens opacity
e: In Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI), 12-lead ECG showing ST-segment elevation and elevated cardiac Troponin I provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (crushing substernal chest pain radiating to left arm/jaw unrelieved by nitroglycerin).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Left-Sided Heart Failure?
o: 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines and plasma free metanephrines plus adrenal CT/MRI
Macrocytic anemia (MCV >100 fL), hypersegmented neutrophils, low serum B12, and elevated methylmalonic acid
MRI of affected bone (most sensitive early imaging) and bone biopsy with culture
Transthoracic echocardiogram showing reduced LVEF and elevated BNP (>100 pg/mL)
e: In Left-Sided Heart Failure, Transthoracic echocardiogram showing reduced LVEF and elevated BNP (>100 pg/mL) provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and bilateral pulmonary crackles).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Right-Sided Heart Failure (Cor Pulmonale)?
o: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing lens opacity
MRI of affected bone (most sensitive early imaging) and bone biopsy with culture
Echocardiography showing right ventricular dilation and elevated pulmonary artery pressure
NS1 antigen (Days 1–5), IgM ELISA (after Day 5), and serial hematocrit/platelet monitoring
e: In Right-Sided Heart Failure (Cor Pulmonale), Echocardiography showing right ventricular dilation and elevated pulmonary artery pressure provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (jugular venous distension, dependent pitting edema, hepatomegaly, and ascites).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Infective Endocarditis?
o: Blood glucose >600 mg/dL, serum osmolality >320 mOsm/kg, arterial pH >7.30, and minimal ketones
Three sets of blood cultures from separate sites plus transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)
Microcytic hypochromic RBCs on smear, low serum ferritin (most sensitive), and high TIBC
Clinical history plus brain MRI to rule out vascular compression or demyelination
e: In Infective Endocarditis, Three sets of blood cultures from separate sites plus transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (persistent fever, new regurgitant heart murmur, osler nodes, janeway lesions, and roth spots).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Cardiac Tamponade?
o: Bedside transthoracic echocardiogram showing pericardial effusion with right ventricular diastolic collapse
Digital rectal exam showing smooth symmetrical enlargement, PSA to exclude cancer, and post-void residual volume
AP and lateral pelvic/hip radiographs
Clinical diagnosis (wound cultures are frequently negative)
e: In Cardiac Tamponade, Bedside transthoracic echocardiogram showing pericardial effusion with right ventricular diastolic collapse provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (beck's triad: hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and distended neck veins with pulsus paradoxus).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)?
o: Clinical diagnosis (elevated serum tryptase confirms retrospectively — NEVER delay epinephrine)
High-resolution CT (HRCT) chest showing 'signet-ring' dilated airways
12-lead ECG showing ST-segment elevation and elevated cardiac Troponin I
Venous duplex compression ultrasonography and D-dimer assay
e: In Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT), Venous duplex compression ultrasonography and D-dimer assay provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (unilateral calf swelling, warmth, erythema, and tenderness along the deep venous system).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Acute Pulmonary Embolism?
o: CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA)
Joint fluid aspiration showing needle-shaped negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals
Corrected serum calcium >10.5 mg/dL, intact PTH, and ECG showing shortened QT interval
Echocardiography showing right ventricular dilation and elevated pulmonary artery pressure
e: In Acute Pulmonary Embolism, CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (sudden-onset pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea, tachycardia, hemoptysis, and unexplained hypoxemia).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Acute Pericarditis?
o: Elevated bilirubin/INR, low albumin, abdominal ultrasound, and FibroScan/liver biopsy
Serum lipase (>3x upper limit of normal — most specific) and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT
12-lead ECG showing diffuse concave ST-segment elevation and PR-segment depression
Venous duplex compression ultrasonography and D-dimer assay
e: In Acute Pericarditis, 12-lead ECG showing diffuse concave ST-segment elevation and PR-segment depression provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (sharp pleuritic substernal chest pain relieved by leaning forward and pericardial friction rub).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Hypertensive Emergency?
o: Fundoscopy, 12-lead ECG, serum creatinine, troponin, and head CT if neurological signs present
Blood glucose >250 mg/dL, arterial pH <7.30, HCO3 <18 mEq/L, and positive serum/urine ketones
Prolonged aPTT with normal PT, normal platelet count, and low Factor VIII assay
eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73m2 for >3 months and small echogenic kidneys on ultrasound
e: In Hypertensive Emergency, Fundoscopy, 12-lead ECG, serum creatinine, troponin, and head CT if neurological signs present provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (severely elevated bp (>180/120 mmhg) accompanied by acute target-organ damage (encephalopathy, papilledema, aki)).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Acute Aortic Dissection?
o: Macrocytic anemia (MCV >100 fL), hypersegmented neutrophils, low serum B12, and elevated methylmalonic acid
CT angiography of the chest and abdomen (or TEE if unstable)
Blood glucose >250 mg/dL, arterial pH <7.30, HCO3 <18 mEq/L, and positive serum/urine ketones
Intracompartmental pressure measurement (>30 mmHg) alongside clinical 6 Ps assessment
e: In Acute Aortic Dissection, CT angiography of the chest and abdomen (or TEE if unstable) provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (sudden severe 'tearing' chest pain radiating to the interscapular back with asymmetric arm blood pressures).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans)?
o: Clinical exam plus skin biopsy showing full-thickness epidermal necrosis
Venous duplex compression ultrasonography and D-dimer assay
Segmental arterial Doppler and angiography showing corkscrew collaterals
Sputum AFB smear microscopy and Cartridge-Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test (CBNAAT/GeneXpert)
e: In Buerger Disease (Thromboangiitis Obliterans), Segmental arterial Doppler and angiography showing corkscrew collaterals provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (intermittent claudication of feet/hands, rest pain, and digital ulcers in young heavy male smokers).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Varicose Veins & Chronic Venous Insufficiency?
o: Serum sodium <135 mEq/L, low serum osmolality (<275), and inappropriately high urine osmolality (>100)
Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP — most specific) and Rheumatoid Factor (RF) with elevated ESR/CRP
CBC with differential (ANC <500), two sets of blood cultures, and chest X-ray
Venous duplex ultrasound and Trendelenburg retrograde filling test
e: In Varicose Veins & Chronic Venous Insufficiency, Venous duplex ultrasound and Trendelenburg retrograde filling test provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (tortuous dilated superficial leg veins, evening ankle edema, and brownish hemosiderin stasis dermatitis).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming COPD Exacerbation?
o: Spirometry showing post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC <0.70 and ABG showing respiratory acidosis
Low morning serum cortisol, elevated ACTH, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia

MRI of affected bone (most sensitive early imaging) and bone biopsy with culture

Segmental arterial Doppler and angiography showing corkscrew collaterals
24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines and plasma free metanephrines plus adrenal CT/MRI

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Tumor Lysis Syndrome (Oncology Emergency)?

Intraventricular catheter (EVD) ICP monitoring (>20 mmHg sustained) and head CT

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Compartment Syndrome (Orthopedic Emergency)?

Intracompartmental pressure measurement (>30 mmHg) alongside clinical 6 Ps assessment
Markedly suppressed TSH with elevated free T3/T4 and Burch-Wartofsky clinical score

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Fat Embolism Syndrome (Long-Bone Fracture)?

CT angiography of the chest and abdomen (or TEE if unstable)
Two sets of blood cultures, serum lactate, procalcitonin, and SOFA score >=2

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Hip Fracture & Total Hip Arthroplasty?

Immediate non-contrast head CT to rule out intracranial hemorrhage before thrombolysis
Clinical diagnosis confirmed by robust motor response to levodopa
Elevated bilirubin/INR, low albumin, abdominal ultrasound, and FibroScan/liver biopsy

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Osteomyelitis?
o: Markedly suppressed TSH with elevated free T3/T4 and Burch-Wartofsky clinical score
Clinical inspection showing silvery plaques, nail pitting, and Koebner phenomenon
MRI of affected bone (most sensitive early imaging) and bone biopsy with culture

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Rheumatoid Arthritis?

Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP — most specific) and Rheumatoid Factor (RF) with elevated ESR/CRP
e: In Rheumatoid Arthritis, Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP — most specific) and Rheumatoid Factor (RF) with elevated ESR/CRP provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (symmetric morning joint stiffness >1 hour affecting mcp/pip joints, ulnar deviation, and swan-neck/boutonniere deformities).

12-lead ECG showing ST-segment elevation and elevated cardiac Troponin I

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Gout (Acute Gouty Arthritis)?

Immediate non-contrast head CT to rule out intracranial hemorrhage before thrombolysis
Clinical diagnosis (elevated serum tryptase confirms retrospectively — NEVER delay epinephrine)

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Anaphylactic Shock?

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Septic Shock?

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Acute Angle-Closure Glaucoma?

Serum potassium <3.5 mEq/L and 12-lead ECG
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing lens opacity

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Retinal Detachment?

Audiometry showing low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and clinical exclusion of acoustic neuroma

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Meniere Disease?

Serum sodium <135 mEq/L, serum osmolality, urine sodium, and volume status assessment
Prolonged aPTT with normal PT, normal platelet count, and low Factor VIII assay
e: In Meniere Disease, Audiometry showing low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and clinical exclusion of acoustic neuroma provides definitive diagnostic confirmation alongside clinical presentation (episodic triad of severe spinning vertigo, unilateral fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, and roaring tinnitus).

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Cataract & Post-Cataract Surgery?

Chest X-ray showing blunting of costophrenic angle and diagnostic thoracentesis (Light's criteria)

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Tetanus (Clostridium tetani)?

Immediate non-contrast head CT to rule out intracranial hemorrhage before thrombolysis

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Psoriasis Vulgaris?

Prolonged aPTT with normal PT, normal platelet count, and low Factor VIII assay

q: Which diagnostic investigation or finding is the primary standard for confirming Hypokalemia (Serum K+ <3.5 mEq/L)?
